title: Launch microtasks scratchpad - hosted API v2 rollout
content:
Morning quick log (3/13) - brain dump / todo.

High level goal: ship hosted API v2 rollout (canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with updated model routing, cost controls, and streaming improvements. Keep latency SLOs stable and ensure fallback meshes for capacity constraints.

PRD edit notes (to finish before 3/15):
- Add section: 'Fallback routing behavior' with concrete examples: if p95 > 350ms for 2 minutes then route to cheaper model-compact-1 (owner: Jonah).
- Clarify rollout metric definitions: use p95 latency, token-cost per 1k tokens, error-rate (5xx + model-timeouts).
- Add migration notes for existing API keys: show opt-in flag vs auto-upgrade schedule.
- Include sample request/response for streaming + function-calling combo (small example snippet).
- Tiny UX note: default batching policy set to 'auto' for new orgs, but needs opt-out path.

Today sprint microtasks (priority ordering):
1) Confirm canary dashboard panel with observability: make sure traces show selected model variant tag (Maya, due EOD).
2) Finalize release notes draft (bullet list) and send to comms for review (Aisha, due 3/14 11:00am).
3) Runbook: add step for 'increase dedicated capacity' and rollback commands (Ethan, link to doc CONFLUENCE-1234).
4) Legal check: confirm no new data retention exposures with streaming changes (Ping Legal slack, cc Maya).
5) Update quickstart snippet in docs to use streaming token flush example (owner: me).

Meeting notes + action items:
- 09:00 eng sync with serving-runtime team: kernel-selection changes look fine; ask: will new kernel change memory footprint for 8k context? (Jonah to confirm, reply by 3/13).
- 10:30 SRE call: autoscaler cooldown tweak recommended from 60s -> 45s during canary window; action: SRE to monitor CPU/GPU util 3/13-3/15.
- 13:00 CS briefing: update on opt-in vs forced upgrade. CS wants a one-pager for customers with high throughput (Maya owns).

Launch checklist (quick, iterative):
- Pre-launch
  - [ ] Feature flag gates created for org-level opt-in (done: feature-flag fg-hosted-v2 created)
  - [x] Canary hosts provisioned (region: us-west1)
  - [ ] Billing: confirm rate-limit quota defaults and overridable by account (Finance meeting scheduled 3/14)
  - [ ] Documentation: migration guide draft ready (target 3/14)

- During canary (0-10%)
  - [ ] Nightly smoke tests run on canary (automated)
  - [ ] Latency/Errors dashboard alerts configured (pager on-call if p95 > 400ms)
  - [ ] Fallback routing verified between model-alpha -> model-compact-1 (test plan in linked_artifacts)

- Rollout steps
  - [ ] 10% -> wait 12 hours -> check metrics
  - [ ] 50% -> wait 24 hours -> check metrics and cost delta
  - [ ] 100% -> final sweep, close rollout ticket

Post-launch items:
- Run evals on representative prompt set (run the Redwood-optimize workload; schedule with Applied ML).
- Billing reconciliation: confirm per-token rates for embedded streaming tokens.
- Retro meeting schedule: 3/20 10:00am (add to calendar).

Risks / open questions (notes to self):
- Will default 'auto' batching push some low-latency customers into higher p95? Need a regression test.
- Model-compact-1 output quality vs model-alpha: get small evals on safety/accuracy.
- Are there any SLA language changes for hosted customers if we introduce aggressive fallback? (Legal + Sales ask)

Small debugging snippets and quick commands (for my memory):
- Query to validate rollout tag in logs: trace.search("metadata.model_variant:hosted-v2") — check p95 by trace.
- Smoke command for sample streaming: curl -X POST /v2/generate -d '{"stream":true, "model":"model-alpha"}' --truncated example (update docs snip).

Notes to self (short):
- Keep email short when pinging execs: 1 line summary + 3 bullets impact / mitigation / ask.
- Focus on two metrics: p95 latency and cost delta per 100k tokens. Everything else is secondary for this rollout.

People to ping later: Jonas@infra (kernel mem), Priya@applied-ml (evals), Legal intake channel.

End-of-day reflection: I feel like the PRD still needs a single clearly-stated rollback criterion (write one-liner). Also need to reduce doc clutter by centralizing links in the PRD 'references' section.

-- scratchpad ends --
